channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Trump Awards Rudy Giuliani With Presidential Medal of Freedom
item.description: President Donald Trump awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom to former New York Mayor Rudy Giuliani, bestowing the nation’s highest civilian honor on the once celebrated figure who later helped spearhead efforts to overturn the results of the 2020 presidential election.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Subramanian

item.title: Progressive Democrats in House Push Back on Energy Permitting Bill
item.description: A growing chorus of progressive lawmakers in the US House oppose legislation to speed the federal approval process for major energy projects, underscoring the division among Congressional Democrats.
item.dc:creator: Ari Natter

item.title: Colombian President Vows Retaliation After Villavicencio Car Bomb Attack
item.description: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella vowed revenge on the perpetrators of a car bomb attack that devastated the regional government headquarters in the nation’s biggest oil-producing province.
item.dc:creator: Oscar Medina

item.title: US Army Orders Weapons Storage Review Ahead of Iowa Explosion
item.description: The US Army has ordered a review of its weapons storage facilities nationwide after the discovery of dangerously deteriorated explosives at an Iowa ammunition plant raised concerns about potential lead contamination in surrounding communities.
item.dc:creator: Jen Judson and Courtney McBride

item.title: Russia to Respond to Ukraine’s Attacks on Refineries, Putin Says
item.description: Moscow will respond to Ukraine’s ongoing attacks on oil refineries, with the situation on Russian domestic fuel market remaining challenging, according to President Vladimir Putin.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: RFK Jr.’s Calendars Unveiled as Part of US Health Record Release
item.description: The US Department of Health and Human Services launched a website hosting more than 92,000 documents including Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s calendars and agency correspondence during the Covid-19 pandemic, in what the HHS called a push for greater transparency.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Nix

item.title: Nvidia Drama 'Screams for Significant Investigations,' Says Admiral Stavridis
item.description: After a week of whiplash over Jensen Huang’s future and new US chip curbs, Beijing sent a clear message to Washington about their trade truce: China is holding up its side of the bargain — for now. That decision was seen as an important test of a detente between the world’s largest economies after the US this month imposed new rules to limit Chinese access to advanced semiconductors. Admiral James Stavaridis, Retired US Navy Admiral and Bloomberg Opinion columnist, discusses the national security risks associated with Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, developments in the war in Iran, and the latest from Ukraine. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Pentagon Inspector General Plans Major Audit as Probes Loom
item.description: The Pentagon’s inspector general is launching a major audit of the department’s defense contracts, loans and equity stakes to see whether procedures were followed, as Democrats in Congress vow to investigate the Trump administration over alleged conflicts of interest.
item.dc:creator: Tony Capaccio

item.title: Van Hollen’s Schumer Challenge Fuels Push for Bolder Democratic Agenda
item.description: Progressive Chris Van Hollen’s challenge to Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer raises pressure on the incoming congressional majority to take bolder action to rein in corporate power and confront Donald Trump, even if the bid fails.
item.dc:creator: Steven T. Dennis

item.title: US Set to Raise Tariffs on China, EU and Others
item.description: The US is said to be preparing to announce it will raise tariffs on goods from China, the European Union and more than a dozen other economies. The Trump administration has been trying to block cheap foreign goods from flooding American markets. Bloomberg's Tyler Kendall reports from the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Switzerland’s Frozen Russian Asset Haul Climbs Above $10 Billion
item.description: The value of Russian assets frozen by Switzerland climbed to 8.5 billion Swiss francs ($10.2 billion) as the nation continues to adopt the European Union sanctions imposed on politicians, business tycoons and companies close to the Kremlin.
item.dc:creator: Hugo Miller

item.title: Gaza Peace-Board Envoy Blames Netanyahu for Stalling Trump Deal
item.description: A representative of the US-led Board of Peace accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of holding up the long-dormant plan to end the war in Gaza.
item.dc:creator: Dan Williams

item.title: South Africa Sentences Russia Army Recruit as Ukraine Urges Action
item.description: A South African court sentenced a Zimbabwean arrested while transiting through the country to join Russia’s military campaign against Ukraine, an early sign of a crackdown on the recruitment of African men to fight in the war.
item.dc:creator: Antony Sguazzin and Volodymyr Verbianyi

item.title: US Readies Tariff Hike on China, EU Goods as Soon as Tuesday
item.description: The US is set to announce as soon as Tuesday plans to raise tariffs on goods from China, the European Union and more than a dozen other economies, according to people familiar with the matter, as the Trump administration moves to replace levies struck down by the Supreme Court.
item.dc:creator: Alicia Diaz and Annmarie Hordern

item.title: Houthi Attack on Riyadh Tower Injures 11 People, Saudis Say
item.description: The Houthis injured 11 people with an attack on a tower in Riyadh’s main business district, Saudi Arabian authorities said, in a further setback to the kingdom’s efforts to establish the capital as a global financial center.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Elimam, Mirette Magdy and Sherif Tarek

item.title: McCormick Warns of ‘Slippery Slope’ After Trump Pressured Nvidia
item.description: Republican Senator Dave McCormick warned that President Donald Trump’s intervention with the Nvidia Corp. board to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive could create a “slippery slope.”
item.dc:creator: Erik Wasson and Annmarie Hordern

item.title: Xi Probes Shanghai Boss, Widening Biggest Shakeup in Decades
item.description: China opened an investigation into Chen Jining, a member of the country’s elite Politburo and the party chief of the financial hub Shanghai — deepening upheaval in the nation’s top leadership as the ruling Communist Party prepares for a reshuffle next year.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Magyar Meets Zelenskyy in Bid to Reset Hungary-Ukraine Relations
item.description: Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar traveled to Ukraine to meet with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, in the latest sign of improving ties between the neighbors after the ouster of Viktor Orban.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Escritt and Zoltan Simon

item.title: Major UK Review Into Welfare Defers Another Spending Question
item.description: Andy Burnham’s government pledged to overhaul the process by which disabled Britons get assessed for welfare payments, while stopping short of setting out how it would curb spending on an issue that’s predicted to cost around £40 billion ($52 billion) by the end of the decade.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain, Joe Mayes and Andrew Atkinson

item.title: Huang Behavior Complaints, Kalshi to Add Stock Trading
item.description: All on the latest episode of "Bloomberg Businessweek Daily." On the show today, Ian King, Bloomberg News US Semiconductor Reporter, Anna Wong, Bloomberg Economics Chief US Economist, Ryan Gould, Bloomberg News Deals Reporter, Mark Gurman, Bloomberg News Managing Editor of Consumer Technology, Michael Ball, Bloomberg News Macro Strategist. (Source: Bloomberg)
